ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The figure above shows a model generated from a study of interactions in a Serengeti ecosystem. This figure describes hypothesized relationships between a parasite that causes disease in wildebeest, rinderpest, and other important components of the ecosystem. Thick arrows represent dominant effects, and “grass” is in a dotted circle because that variable was not directly measured in the study.1. Which of the following can most reasonably be predicted based on this figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Increasing the amount of rinderpest could indirectly lower tree numbers.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ecosystem causal relationship model, containing nodes such as Rinderpest, Wildebeest, Grass, Fire, Trees, etc. In the figure, the arrow from Rinderpest to Wildebeest is marked with a negative sign; a negative relationship is shown between Wildebeest and Grass; the relationship from Grass to Fire is positive; the relationship from Fire to Trees is negative. Reasoning: Propagating the signs along this chain, increasing rinderpest will decrease wildebeest; the decrease in wildebeest will reduce the consumption of grass, causing grass to increase; the increase in grass will cause fire to increase; the increase in fire will decrease trees. Therefore, increasing rinderpest may reduce the number of trees through this indirect path.
